newsitem.title: INDIA: India 95/96 GDP growth rises to 7.0 pct vs 6.3-RBI.
newsitem.headline: India 95/96 GDP growth rises to 7.0 pct vs 6.3-RBI.

text.p: Gross domestic product (GDP) grew at seven percent in 1995/96 (April-March) against 6.3 percent in 1994/95, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said in its annual report for 1995/96 (July-June) on Friday.
This was largely due to a strong 12.1 percent growth in the industrial sector in 1995/96, the report said.
Capacity utilisation in the manufacturing sector went up from 80.3 percent in 1993/94 to 82.0 percent in 1994/95 and declined marginally to 81.9 percent in 1995/96, the RBI said.
The RBI however cautioned that more reforms were needed if the rate of growth were to be sustained.
"One of the most serious potential constraints to the achievement of high industrial growth in India on a sustained basis relates to the availability of adequate infrastructure," the RBI said.

"Besides infrastructure development, suitable institutional and legal reforms are necessary to ensure the efficient functioning of market forces and to make the process of industrial restructuring dynamic and self-sustaining."
